title: The wooden flute
text:
Every evening, old Pak Hasan sat on his porch and played a wooden flute. The soft music floated over the rice fields, and the neighbours loved to listen.

Rudi, who lived next door, was eight years old. He had never held a flute in his life, but he longed to play one. One afternoon, he crept to the porch and asked, "Pak Hasan, will you teach me?"

Pak Hasan smiled. "Music is like a seed," he said. "You plant it, you water it every day, and slowly it grows." He handed Rudi the flute.

Rudi blew as hard as he could. A loud, squeaky noise shot out. A hen in the yard flapped her wings and ran away. Rudi's cheeks turned pink. "I am no good at this," he muttered.

"Not yet," said Pak Hasan kindly. "Try again, but blow gently, as if you were blowing on hot tea."

Rudi tried again. This time, a thin, wobbly note came out. It was not beautiful, but it was a real note. Rudi grinned from ear to ear.

Every day after school, Rudi practised on the porch. After a few weeks his notes were smooth. After a few months he could play a whole song.

On Pak Hasan's birthday, Rudi stood on the porch and played his favourite song for the whole village. When he finished, everybody clapped. Pak Hasan wiped his eyes. "My little seed has grown," he said.
